key_insight: Nahual unifies language and 3D molecular generation in one decoder-only model, combining text-based control with native coordinate generation.
engineering_relevance: A single model could support workflows spanning molecular conformer search, microsolvation, crystal structure prediction, and adsorption on metal surfaces.
method: Uses a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion architecture for sequences mixing text and 3D molecules.
Introduces next-token diffusion: a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to preceding clean tokens, without expanding context size.
Trains one shared set of weights end to end across twelve 3D chemistry tasks.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on a curated twelve-task dataset with task-specific metrics and baselines, reporting performance beyond specialized state-of-the-art models for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational cost or generalization beyond the curated tasks, leaving deployment efficiency and broader transfer uncertain.
paper_title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
